You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From 4b41a9d0fe3db5f91078a380f62f0572c3ecf2dd Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Miaoqian Lin <linmq006@gmail.com>
Date: Sat, 8 Jan 2022 09:59:31 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] soc: qcom: aoss: Fix missing put_device call in qmp_get

The reference taken by 'of_find_device_by_node()' must be released when
not needed anymore.
Add the corresponding 'put_device()' in the error handling paths.

Fixes: 8c75d585b931 ("soc: qcom: aoss: Expose send for generic usecase")
Signed-off-by: Miaoqian Lin <linmq006@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Stephen Boyd <swboyd@chromium.org>
Signed-off-by: Bjorn Andersson <bjorn.andersson@linaro.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220108095931.21527-1-linmq006@gmail.com
---
 drivers/soc/qcom/qcom_aoss.c | 6 +++++-
 1 file changed, 5 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/drivers/soc/qcom/qcom_aoss.c b/drivers/soc/qcom/qcom_aoss.c
index cbe5e39fdaeb..563ae0a501dc 100644
--- a/drivers/soc/qcom/qcom_aoss.c
+++ b/drivers/soc/qcom/qcom_aoss.c
@@ -451,7 +451,11 @@ struct qmp *qmp_get(struct device *dev)
 
 	qmp = platform_get_drvdata(pdev);
 
-	return qmp ? qmp : ERR_PTR(-EPROBE_DEFER);
+	if (!qmp) {
+		put_device(&pdev->dev);
+		return ERR_PTR(-EPROBE_DEFER);
+	}
+	return qmp;
 }
 EXPORT_SYMBOL(qmp_get);
 
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by a missing call to `put_device()` in the error handling path of the `qmp_get` function. When `of_find_device_by_node()` is called, it increments the device's reference count, and if the function subsequently fails to retrieve the expected data (indicated by a null `qmp`), the reference count was not decremented, leading to a potential memory leak. The patch adds the necessary `put_device()` call to ensure that the reference is released when the device is no longer needed, thus preventing resource leaks.
